description: Crew Vital is a two-person team using AI, data analytics, and research to support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. We aim to build a smart health-monitoring system that combines key health indicators, detects meaningful changes, and helps astronauts understand what needs attention and what to check next.
summary:
Crew Vital is an AI-powered Mission Medic designed to support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. We developed a Human–Habitat Health Twin that analyzes astronaut health signals, crew-wide patterns, spacecraft environmental conditions, mission constraints, and sensor reliability together.

Instead of only showing abnormal readings, Crew Vital reasons across multiple possible causes, measures uncertainty, and recommends the next best check that can reduce uncertainty with the least crew effort. It can also distinguish between an individual health issue and a shared habitat problem, verify whether sensor data is trustworthy, and adapt recommendations based on communication delay, available onboard tools, and mission workload.

This addresses the challenge by helping astronauts assess their own health and decide what to check or do next when immediate Earth-based medical support may not be available. Crew Vital is important because future deep-space crews will need greater autonomy, faster evidence-based decisions, and safer use of limited onboard medical and environmental resources.
details:
Crew Vital is an AI-powered Mission Medic designed to support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. The system combines a Human Health Twin, Habitat Twin, crew-wide pattern detection, sensor reliability checks, and mission constraints into one adaptive decision-support workflow.

Crew Vital does more than display health data. It analyzes changes in indicators such as heart rate, sleep, stress, recovery, SpO₂, and environmental factors such as cabin CO₂, temperature, humidity, and radiation context. When several explanations are possible, the system keeps multiple hypotheses open and recommends the next best measurement based on expected information gain and crew effort. After a new measurement is entered, Crew Vital updates its reasoning, recommends an appropriate onboard action, and supports rechecking the situation.

The system can also detect whether similar symptoms across multiple crew members may point to a shared habitat problem rather than separate individual health issues. It includes sensor-integrity logic to help prevent one questionable reading from driving a decision. Mission constraints such as communication delay, available onboard tools, crew time, and workload are also considered.

We developed the prototype using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, and GitHub. Synthetic health and habitat data are used for demonstration.

The creative aspect of Crew Vital is its closed-loop reasoning approach: Observe → Reason → Verify → Measure → Act → Recheck. Our intended impact is to support greater astronaut autonomy, reduce unnecessary testing, improve use of limited onboard resources, and help crews make safer evidence-based decisions when immediate Earth-based medical support is unavailable.
